claim: Generation of skeletal muscle cells with human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) opens new avenues for deciphering essential, but poorly understood aspects of transcriptional regulation in human myogenic specification.
source: Generation of skeletal muscle cells with human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) opens new avenues for deciphering essential, but poorly understood aspects of transcriptional regulation in human myogenic specification.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of hPSC-based skeletal muscle generation for research purposes, representing the authors' perspective on the field.

claim: The study characterized the transcriptional landscape of distinct human myogenic stages, including OCT4::EGFP+ pluripotent stem cells, MSGN1::EGFP+ presomite cells, PAX7::EGFP+ skeletal muscle progenitor cells, MYOG::EGFP+ myoblasts, and multinucleated myotubes.
source: In this study, we characterized the transcriptional landscape of distinct human myogenic stages, including OCT4::EGFP+ pluripotent stem cells, MSGN1::EGFP+ presomite cells, PAX7::EGFP+ skeletal muscle progenitor cells, MYOG::EGFP+ myoblasts, and multinucleated myotubes.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and cell populations analyzed in the study.

claim: Signature gene expression profiles were defined from each isolated cell population with unbiased clustering analysis.
source: We defined signature gene expression profiles from each isolated cell population with unbiased clustering analysis, which provided unique insights into the transcriptional dynamics of human myogenesis from undifferentiated hPSCs to fully differentiated myotubes.
evidence: This describes the analytical method used to characterize gene expression patterns.

claim: TWIST1 was identified as a critical factor in maintenance of human PAX7::EGFP+ putative skeletal muscle progenitor cells using a knock-out strategy.
source: Using a knock-out strategy, we identified TWIST1 as a critical factor in maintenance of human PAX7::EGFP+ putative skeletal muscle progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a key finding from the knockout experiments described in the study.

claim: The data revealed a new role of TWIST1 in human skeletal muscle progenitors.
source: Our data revealed a new role of TWIST1 in human skeletal muscle progenitors, and we have established a foundation to identify transcriptional regulations of human myogenic ontogeny (online database can be accessed in http://www.myogenesis.net/).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings regarding TWIST1 function.

claim: During embryonic myogenesis, skeletal muscle is generated through multiple cellular stages, including pluripotent preimplanted embryos, somite cells, skeletal muscle stem/precursor cells, proliferating myoblasts, and multinucleated myotubes.
source: During embryonic myogenesis, skeletal muscle is generated through multiple cellular stages, including pluripotent preimplanted embryos, somite cells, skeletal muscle stem/precursor cells, proliferating myoblasts, and multinucleated myotubes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the stages of embryonic muscle development.

claim: Previous studies reported the generation of in vitro skeletal muscle cells with overexpression of exogenous myogenic transcription factors into fibroblasts and stem cells.
source: While previous studies reported the generation of in vitro skeletal muscle cells with overexpression of exogenous myogenic transcription factors (TFs) into fibroblasts and stem cells (Darabi et al., 2012; Tedesco et al., 2012; Albini et al., 2013; Salani et al., 2012; Davis et al., 1987; Magli and Perlingeiro, 2017), they did not provide a step-wise transcriptional blueprint of myogenic specification.
evidence: This references prior work in the field with citations.

claim: Previous studies with overexpression of exogenous myogenic transcription factors did not provide a step-wise transcriptional blueprint of myogenic specification.
source: While previous studies reported the generation of in vitro skeletal muscle cells with overexpression of exogenous myogenic transcription factors (TFs) into fibroblasts and stem cells (Darabi et al., 2012; Tedesco et al., 2012; Albini et al., 2013; Salani et al., 2012; Davis et al., 1987; Magli and Perlingeiro, 2017), they did not provide a step-wise transcriptional blueprint of myogenic specification.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of prior work based on the authors' review of the literature.

claim: Several reports were published that effectively directed hPSCs to human skeletal muscle cell fates.
source: Recently, several reports were published that effectively directed hPSCs to human skeletal muscle cell fates (Chal et al., 2015; Choi et al., 2016; Shelton et al., 2014), which can be a reasonable platform to tease out the transcriptional trajectory of human myogenesis processes.
evidence: This references recent publications with citations.

claim: Heterogenous cellular populations in myogenic cell culture hamper further cellular isolation of specific myogenic cells for detailed studies.
source: However, the heterogenous cellular populations in the myogenic cell culture hamper further cellular isolation of specific myogenic cells for detailed studies.
evidence: This is an observation about a technical challenge in the field.

claim: OCT4 is one of the POU transcription factors that is essential for maintaining pluripotency and self-renewal of PSCs.
source: While OCT4 is one of the POU transcription factors that is essential for maintaining pluripotency and self-renewal of PSCs, MSGN1 has a key function in generation of paraxial mesoderm cells (Loh et al., 2006; Fior et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about OCT4 function, supported by citations.

claim: MSGN1 has a key function in generation of paraxial mesoderm cells.
source: While OCT4 is one of the POU transcription factors that is essential for maintaining pluripotency and self-renewal of PSCs, MSGN1 has a key function in generation of paraxial mesoderm cells (Loh et al., 2006; Fior et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MSGN1 function, supported by citations.

claim: MYOG is a skeletal muscle-specific transcription factor in the basic helix loop helix class of DNA-binding proteins and has a critical role in skeletal muscle differentiation during embryogenesis.
source: MYOG is a skeletal muscle-specific transcription factor in the basic helix loop helix class of DNA-binding proteins and has a critical role in skeletal muscle differentiation during embryogenesis (Nabeshima et al., 1993; Bentzinger et al., 2012; Hasty et al., 1993; Brunetti and Goldfine, 1990; Magli and Perlingeiro, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MYOG function, supported by citations.

claim: PAX7 is a member of the paired box (PAX) family of transcription factors, which has important roles in skeletal muscle development, maintenance, and regeneration.
source: Another major gene is PAX7, a member of the paired box (PAX) family of transcription factors, which has important roles in skeletal muscle development, maintenance, and regeneration (Bentzinger et al., 2012; Seale et al., 2000; Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2005; Parker et al., 2003; Biressi et al., 2007; Buckingham and Relaix, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PAX7 function, supported by citations.

claim: Previous reports with genetic reporter mice showed the transcriptional profiles of PAX3 or PAX7 expressing cells in embryonic and postnatal muscle tissues.
source: Previous reports with genetic reporter mice showed the transcriptional profiles of PAX3 or PAX7 expressing cells in embryonic and postnatal muscle tissues (Relaix et al., 2005; Tichy et al., 2018), which presented developmental transcriptional changes in a specific population.
evidence: This references prior work with mouse models, supported by citations.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has been developed and used widely in genetic modification of hPSCs due to its simplified design and feasibility.
source: Recently, the CRISPR/Cas9 system has been developed and used widely in genetic modification of hPSCs due to its simplified design and feasibility (Mali et al., 2013; Cong et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CRISPR/Cas9 technology, supported by citations.

claim: A 'knock-in' strategy to generate a genetic reporter hPSC line using the CRISPR/Cas9 system is now feasible and enables prospective isolation of homogenous cell populations.
source: For instance, a 'knock-in' strategy to generate a genetic reporter hPSC line using the CRISPR/Cas9 system is now feasible and enables us to purify a homogenous cell population by prospective isolation (Ganat et al., 2012; Tchieu et al., 2017; Mukherjee et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes an established technique, supported by citations.

claim: Multiple genetic reporter hPSC lines for stage-specific transcription factors can provide a step-wise transcriptional landscape for a certain lineage.
source: Moreover, multiple genetic reporter hPSC lines for stage-specific transcription factors can provide a step-wise transcriptional landscape for a certain lineage.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the utility of multiple reporter lines.

claim: The study conducted step-wise isolations of stage-specific cellular subtypes during muscle differentiation in vitro and performed global gene expression analysis.
source: In this study, to systematically investigate the transcriptional blueprint for developing human skeletal muscle cells and to gain comprehensive insights into the molecular signatures of putative skeletal muscle stem/progenitors, we conducted step-wise isolations of stage-specific cellular subtypes during muscle differentiation in vitro and performed global gene expression analysis.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach of the study.

claim: Five distinct cell types in human embryonic myogenesis were isolated, including OCT4::EGFP+ embryonic stem cells, MSGN1::EGFP+ presomite cells, PAX7::EGFP+ putative skeletal muscle stem/precursor cells, MYOG::EGFP+ myoblast cells, and multinucleated myotubes.
source: Using our human genetic reporter PSC lines and a newly devised method for myotube enrichment, we isolated five distinct cell types in human embryonic myogenesis, including OCT4::EGFP+ embryonic stem cells, MSGN1::EGFP+ presomite cells, PAX7::EGFP+ putative skeletal muscle stem/precursor cells, MYOG::EGFP+ myoblast cells, and multinucleated myotubes (Loh et al., 2006; Fior et al., 2012; Nichols et al., 1998; Seale et al., 2000; Hasty et al., 1993).
evidence: This describes the experimental results of cell isolation.

claim: The clustering analysis presented transcriptional changes during in vitro muscle generation.
source: The clustering analysis presented transcriptional changes during in vitro muscle generation, and we identified several transcription factors that have key roles in human myogenesis in vitro.
evidence: This describes the results of the clustering analysis.

claim: Several transcription factors that have key roles in human myogenesis in vitro were identified.
source: The clustering analysis presented transcriptional changes during in vitro muscle generation, and we identified several transcription factors that have key roles in human myogenesis in vitro.
evidence: This describes a finding from the study.

claim: TWIST1 has not been extensively studied in human muscle biology and relevant genetic diseases.
source: One of the transcription factors we identified is TWIST1, which has not been extensively studied in human muscle biology and relevant genetic diseases.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge about TWIST1.

claim: During human embryonic myogenesis, several key marker genes are known to play significant roles in each stage.
source: During human embryonic myogenesis, several key marker genes are known to play significant roles in each stage (Figure 1A), for example, OCT4 and NANOG in pluripotent stem cells, MSGN1 and TBX6 in presomite cells (Chapman and Papaioannou, 1998; Fior et al., 2012; Loh et al., 2006; Thomson et al., 1998), PAX7 in putative myogenic stem/progenitor cells, and MYOD1 and MYOG in myoblasts before myotube formation (Nabeshima et al., 1993; Seale et al., 2000; Hasty et al., 1993; Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge about myogenic marker genes, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: An in vitro myogenic specification protocol was previously developed directing hPSCs into human skeletal muscle cells through the GSK3β and Notch signal inhibition pathway.
source: Previously, we have developed an in vitro myogenic specification protocol directing hPSCs into human skeletal muscle cells through the GSK3β and Notch signal inhibition pathway (Choi et al., 2016).
evidence: This references prior work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: Expression levels of pluripotency markers, OCT4 and NANOG, were high in undifferentiated hESCs, but decreased rapidly upon initiation of muscle specification.
source: Expression levels of pluripotency markers, OCT4 and NANOG, were high in undifferentiated hESCs, but decreased rapidly upon initiation of muscle specification.
evidence: This describes experimental observations from qRT-PCR analysis, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Within 4 days of myogenic specification, the expression of mesoderm markers T (Brachyury), MIXL1, and presomite markers MSGN1 and TBX6 was induced.
source: Within 4 days of myogenic specification, the expression of mesoderm markers T (Brachyury), MIXL1, and presomite markers MSGN1 and TBX6 was induced, while the expression levels of PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1 and MYOG gradually increased around day 20.
evidence: This describes experimental observations from qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: The expression levels of PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1 and MYOG gradually increased around day 20 of myogenic specification.
source: Within 4 days of myogenic specification, the expression of mesoderm markers T (Brachyury), MIXL1, and presomite markers MSGN1 and TBX6 was induced, while the expression levels of PAX7, MYF5, MYOD1 and MYOG gradually increased around day 20.
evidence: This describes experimental observations from qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: PAX3, MEOX1, FOXC1, and FOXC2 gene expression started at Day 4 and had a peak between Day 6 and Day 8, implying that intermediate somite stage fills the gap between MSGN1+ stage and PAX7+ stage.

PAX3, MEOX1, FOXC1, and FOXC2 gene started their gene expression at Day 4, and had a peak between Day 6 and Day 8 which imply that intermediate somite stage fills the gap between MSGN1+ stage and PAX7+ stage.
evidence: This describes experimental observations and interpretation from gene expression profiling.

claim: 96.42 ± 2.55% of undifferentiated hESCs expressed OCT4 protein.
source: Distinct protein expression patterns were observed during our in vitro myogenic specification: OCT4 expressing cells were 96.42 ± 2.55% of undifferentiated hESCs (mean ± SEM); at day 4, 87.78 ± 4.46% of the cell population expressed TBX6; at day 20, 31.72 ± 5.78% of the cell population expressed PAX7; at day 25, 53.30 ± 6.39% of the cell population expressed MYOG; at day 40, 87.99 ± 3.64% of the cell population expressed MF20.
evidence: This describes quantitative immunostaining results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A new method was devised for multinucleated myotube isolation from heterogeneous culture based on differential detachment rates between myotubes and non-myotube cells upon trypsin treatment.
source: For multinucleated myotube isolation from the heterogeneous culture, we devised a new method based on differential detachment rates between myotubes and non-myotube cells upon trypsin treatment. Non-myotube cells tend to detach faster than myotubes, which enabled us to remove non-myotube cells (mostly myoblast-like cells) first, followed by harvesting remnant multinucleated myotubes a few minutes later (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: This describes a novel method developed in the study, illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–I.

claim: The remnant cell population after differential trypsin treatment showed enriched gene expression levels of DMD (32.69 ± 1.28 fold changes), TTN (27.42 ± 1.26), and MYH2 (21.40 ± 0.95) compared to the detached cell population.
source: We confirmed that the remnant cell population showed enriched gene expression levels of DMD (32.69 ± 1.28 fold changes), TTN (27.42 ± 1.26), and MYH2 (21.40 ± 0.95) compared to the detached cell population (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This describes qRT-PCR validation of the myotube isolation method, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J.

claim: Each FACS purified population showed high levels of expression of the representative marker genes for the corresponding stage of differentiation.
source: Each FACS purified population was validated using qRT-PCR (Figure 1E), and the results confirmed that each cell population showed high levels of expression of the representative marker genes for the corresponding stage of differentiation: OCT4 and NANOG in OCT4::EGFP+ cells, TBX6, T, and MSGN1 in MSGN1::EGFP+ cells, PAX3 and PAX7 in PAX7::EGFP+ cells, MYOD1, MYOG, MEF2C, MYH2, and TTN in MYOG::EGFP+ cells, and MEF2C, MYH2, and TTN in isolated myotubes.
evidence: This describes qRT-PCR validation results shown in Figure 1E.

source: In order to comprehensively examine stage-specific gene expression profiles during in vitro human myogenesis at the genome-wide level, we carried out RNA Sequencing (RNA-seq) of the purified cells from five different stages of myogenesis: OCT4::EGFP+ cells, MSGN1::EGFP+ cells, PAX7::EGFP+ cells, MYOG::EGFP+ cells, and Myotubes.
